title: Refuse batch starts that never happen

blocks.text: Operators type the start of each batch run as a local date and time in the data centre's zone, and `BatchStarts` turns it into the moment the job queue receives. Twice a year the operations team finds a run in the wrong place: in spring a run they set for a time that night started later than they typed, without anyone being asked, and in autumn the nightly export started while the hour it reads was still being written.
The team's rules for the nights the clocks change:

items: a start at a local time that doesn't happen that night is refused with `IllegalArgumentException`, so the operator picks another;
a start at a local time that happens twice runs at the second one, after the clocks have gone back, when the hour's data is complete.

blocks.text: Every other start runs at the time typed. Finish `startOf` in `src/main/java/practice/BatchStarts.java`. About four lines in total. The data centres include zones whose clocks change by less than an hour.

cases.says: a local time that happens once, including on the day of a clock change, starts as written with the zone's offset
the job queue receives the instant of the start
a local time in a spring-forward gap is refused with IllegalArgumentException instead of being moved
a local time in an autumn overlap starts at its second occurrence, with the later offset
a zone whose clocks skip half an hour has a gap too, and a time inside it is refused

origin.section: Near a Clock Change a Local Time Can Be Missing or Doubled, and ZonedDateTime Picks One Without Telling You

concepts: ZonedDateTime.of moves a local time in a gap later by the gap's length and takes the earlier offset in an overlap, without an exception; getValidOffsets tells the cases apart so the code can decide.
